assumptions: The object is addressed by its field offsets only; no meaning is assigned to the object or to its +0x18/+0x70 fields.
The raiser's incoming value is a 32-bit quantity: callers load it into esi, which zero-extends, and the leaf compares and stores 32-bit quantities only.
The getter at 0x5f97841 receives rdi = the qword at [rbx+0x40] carried unchanged along the jump path from 0x5f96161: the block at 0x5f9782c writes only rax and r14 before the call.
A missing field is a modelling gap, not a binary behavior: the model raises ValueError, while the binary would read whatever bytes lie at that address.

census.note: Four direct calls to the +0x70 getter (0x5d8d0c0), one to the +0x70 raiser (0x5d8d0d0), three to the +0x18 getter (0x5d8d0e0); no tail jumps, no stored qwords, no RELATIVE addends.

distinct_from: Open PR #2378 (record-fill 0x5f6eb50): that routine is the caller of the getter at 0x5f6eb88, not the getter itself, and #2378 explicitly left the getter's semantics unclaimed.
Open PR #2374 (advance/max leaves 0x5f6f400/0x5f6f430): those are the later leaves of the shared sequence at 0x5f9dfb1/0x5f9dfc1/0x5f9dfd1, not the raiser at 0x5f9dfa1.
No open PR title hit for 5d8d0c0, 5d8d0d0 or 5d8d0e0.

fields.rule: read by the getter at 0x5d8d0c0 (zero-extended to 64 bits); raised to the unsigned 32-bit maximum with the incoming esi value by the raiser at 0x5d8d0d0
read by the getter at 0x5d8d0e0 and returned in rax; never written by any of the three leaves

leaves.rule: obj+0x70 = max(obj+0x70, esi) as unsigned 32-bit quantities; equality stores nothing
leaves.takes: object in rdi, value in esi
leaves.writes: obj+0x70 only, and only when the incoming value is strictly greater

not_claimed: Caller semantics beyond the eight sites; what the objects, the +0x40 subobjects, or the +0x18/+0x70 fields denote.
What happens on any branch target past a site, and the following call at 0x5f9ab06 beyond its argument setup.
Any relation between the three leaves beyond their adjacency, their shared +0x70 field for the first two, and the common +0x40-subobject argument shape at the getter and raiser sites.
